mainTopic: Delayed or time-limited הקמה and הפרה of a wife's vow, and how the father and husband share the power over a betrothed נערה's vows
overview: The amud opens with a ladder of 'אם תמצא לומר' questions about a husband who delays his הפרה. What if he says 'it is cancelled for you tomorrow'? What if he says 'it is upheld for you for an hour'? And what if he clearly says 'it is cancelled after an hour'? The whole day stays open for both הקמה and הפרה, so does that last one work? The גמרא tries to prove the answer from a משנה about a husband who answers his wife's נזירות vow with 'ואני'. It then rejects the proof, because 'ואני' counts as upholding the vow forever, so these questions stay unresolved. Next comes a new משנה about a betrothed נערה. If her father dies, the husband does not take over the father's share, but if the husband dies, the father does take over his share. On the other hand, a husband who has fully married her can cancel her vows even when she is a בוגרת, which a father cannot. The גמרא learns the first rule from the פסוק 'בנעריה בית אביה'. רבה then begins to find a source for the father taking over, using the doubled wording 'היו תהיה', and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if the husband says: It is cancelled for you tomorrow?
steps.stepSummary: Building on the earlier question, the גמרא asks about a husband who says the vow is cancelled starting tomorrow. Does that count as upholding it today, or does it work as a cancellation starting today?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you decide that an unspoken cancellation does not count, what if he said: 'It is cancelled for you tomorrow'? Do we say he cannot cancel tomorrow, because by not cancelling today he has already upheld the vow? Or do we say that since he never said 'it is upheld for you today,' his words 'cancelled tomorrow' really mean cancelled from today?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new follow-up question. A husband says his wife's vow is cancelled 'tomorrow.' Does that work?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband may only do הפרה on the day he hears the vow. If he says 'cancelled tomorrow,' maybe he has let the day pass and so upheld the vow. Or maybe, since he never said he upholds it, we read his words as a cancellation that begins today.

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude that... (opens a follow-up question that assumes one answer to the last question)
It is cancelled for you (the husband's words of הפרה)
It is upheld for you (the husband's words of הקמה)
Do we say... or perhaps... (lays out the two sides of a question)
He is able to cancel

steps.confusionAlert: 'הא לא אמר לה' at the start points back to the question just before this one, about a husband who said 'it is upheld for you today.' It means: if we decide that since he did not say 'cancelled,' nothing was cancelled.

phrases.english: If you conclude that [it stays in force because] he did not say it to her,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier case, where he only said 'it is upheld for you today' and never said 'cancelled.'

phrases.english: Do we say: tomorrow he cannot cancel,
because he has upheld her vow today?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אֲמַר לַהּ
phrases.english: Or perhaps: since he did not say to her
'It is upheld for you today,'

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'cancelled tomorrow' count as upholding the vow today, or as a cancellation that starts today?

steps.title: What if the husband says: It is upheld for you for an hour?
steps.stepSummary: Assuming 'cancelled tomorrow' counts as upholding the vow, the גמרא asks about a husband who says the vow is upheld for only an hour. Is that like saying it is cancelled after the hour?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you decide that even so, since he upheld it today, tomorrow the vow is treated as fully in place, what if he said: 'It is upheld for you for an hour'? Is that like saying 'It is cancelled for you after an hour'? Or perhaps not, since he never actually said that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא climbs one more step up the ladder. It asks about a husband who says the vow is upheld 'for an hour.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Upholding something 'for an hour' seems to hint that it will be cancelled afterward. The question is whether we read that hint as a real הפרה after the hour. Or do we only count what he clearly said, which was upholding?

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
It is treated as if it is already in place
An hour (a short set amount of time)
After an hour

phrases.english: And if you conclude: even so,
since he upheld it today,
tomorrow it is treated as already in place,
if he said to her: 'It is upheld for you for an hour,' what is the law?
Do we say: it is like one who said to her
'It is cancelled for you after an hour'?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: הָא לָא אֲמַר לָהּ?
phrases.english: Or perhaps: he did not say that to her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the strict answer to Step 1 and asks a further question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'upheld for an hour' mean the vow is cancelled once the hour passes?

steps.title: What if he clearly says: It is cancelled after an hour?
steps.stepSummary: Assuming 'upheld for an hour' does not count as cancelling, the גמרא asks about a husband who clearly says the vow is cancelled after an hour. Does holding back for the hour count as upholding, or does it work because the whole day is open for הפרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you decide that since he did not say it, nothing is cancelled, what if he did say to her 'cancelled after an hour'? Do we say that once he upheld it, it stays upheld? Or perhaps, since the whole day is open for both upholding and cancelling, when he says 'It is cancelled for you after an hour,' it works?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the top step of the ladder. The husband clearly says the vow is cancelled after an hour, and the גמרא asks whether that works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says that letting the vow stand for an hour is a real הקמה, and after הקמה there is no more הפרה. The other side says that the whole day of hearing stays open for both הקמה and הפרה, so a cancellation set for later in that same day still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Still, but
Once he upheld it, it is upheld (for good)
Fit for upholding and fit for cancelling
It works / is effective

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the question the גמרא now tries to answer with a proof, so it is the key question of the section.

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר הָא לָא אֲמַר לַהּ,
phrases.english: If you conclude: he did not say it to her,
still, if he did say it to her, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means: what if he clearly said 'It is cancelled for you after an hour'?

phrases.english: Do we say: since he upheld it, it is upheld,
or perhaps: since the whole day
is open for upholding and open for cancelling,
when he says 'It is cancelled for you after an hour,'
it works?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר הָא לָא אֲמַר לַהּ, מִיהוּ אֲמַר לַהּ, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the strict answer to Step 2 and asks the last question in the chain
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a clear, delayed הפרה ('after an hour') work, or does the hour of waiting count as a permanent הקמה?

steps.title: Proof from a husband who answers his wife's נזירות vow with 'And I'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if a wife vows נזירות and her husband says 'ואני,' he can no longer cancel her vow. The גמרא suggests this shows that upholding a vow even for a short time makes it upheld for good.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if she said 'I am a נזירה,' and her husband heard and said 'And I,' he cannot cancel. Why not? Let us say his 'And I' was about himself becoming a נזיר. Her vow 'I am a נזירה' was upheld only for that one moment. After that moment, if he wants to, let him cancel it. So why can he not cancel? Is it not because once he upheld it, it is upheld for good?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to try to answer the question from Step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband says 'ואני,' he leans on his wife's vow, so for that moment he has upheld it. If a short הקמה did not lock it in, he should still be able to cancel later that day. Since the משנה says he cannot, it seems that a short הקמה is permanent. That would answer the question in Step 3: a delayed הפרה does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזירה (a woman's vow of נזירות)
And I (joining someone else's vow)
About himself
Is it not because...? (draws the proof)

phrases.english: Come and hear: [if she said] 'I am hereby a nazirite,'
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת נזיר.

phrases.english: and her husband heard and said 'And I' —
he cannot cancel.
But why not?
Let us say: the 'And I' that he said
was about himself, that he becomes a nazirite,
but her 'I am hereby a nazirite,'
which was upheld for one moment,
phrases.notes: It was upheld only for the moment when he leaned on it to make his own vow.

phrases.english: after that moment, if he wants, let him cancel it.
Why can he not cancel?
Is it not because once he upheld it, it is upheld?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of Step 3
steps.raayaObject: The rule that 'כיון שקיימו קיימו': a short הקמה becomes permanent, so a delayed הפרה does not work
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נזיר: a husband who says 'ואני' to his wife's נזירות vow can no longer cancel it

steps.title: Rejection: 'And I' is like upholding the vow forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The תנא of that משנה holds that saying 'ואני' is like saying 'it is upheld for you forever,' so the case says nothing about a short הקמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He holds that any 'And I' is like one who said: 'It is upheld for you forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof from Step 4, so the question from Step 3 stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if 'ואני' is a short הקמה. The גמרא answers that 'ואני' is really a permanent הקמה. So it is no surprise he cannot cancel later, and we learn nothing about a husband who upholds a vow only for an hour.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (the view of that תנא)
Forever

steps.whatToRemember: The whole ladder of questions (cancelled tomorrow, upheld for an hour, cancelled after an hour) stays unresolved. The 'ואני' case is no proof, because 'ואני' counts as upholding the vow forever.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the rule 'כיון שקיימו קיימו' is wrong. It is only saying the 'ואני' case cannot prove it.

phrases.english: No, he holds:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the תנא of the משנה just quoted.

phrases.english: any 'And I' —
is like one who said 'It is upheld for you forever.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the 'ואני' משנה; the question in Step 3 stays open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'ואני' is a short הקמה, but it actually counts as a permanent הקמה ('קיים ליכי לעולם')

steps.title: When the father dies or the husband dies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the father dies, his power does not pass to the husband. If the husband dies, his power does pass to the father. In this the father is stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the father dies, his authority does not pass to the husband. If the husband dies, his authority passes to the father. In this matter the father's power is stronger than the husband's.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It compares the father and the husband of a betrothed girl when one of them dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נערה המאורסה, the father and the husband must both cancel her vow together. The משנה teaches that this partnership does not work the same in both directions. The father can take over the husband's share, but the husband cannot take over the father's share.

keyTerms.meaning: The authority 'emptied over', meaning it passed fully to the other person
The power is stronger
The father
The husband (here, the man she is betrothed to)

steps.confusionAlert: This is about a betrothed נערה, where father and husband cancel together. It is not about a fully married woman, where the husband cancels alone.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: If the father dies,
phrases.notes: We are talking about a betrothed girl, whose vows need both her father and her husband to cancel them.

phrases.english: the authority does not pass over to the husband.
If the husband dies, the authority passes over to the father.
In this, the father's power is stronger
than the husband's power.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מֵת הָאָב לֹא נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of short-term הקמה ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the father dies, the husband does not take over his share. If the husband dies, the father does take over his share.

steps.title: Where the husband is stronger than the father
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that the husband is stronger in a different way: he can cancel vows once she is a בוגרת, but the father cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: In another matter the husband's power is stronger than the father's: the husband cancels vows when she is a בוגרת, and the father does not cancel vows when she is a בוגרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה balances the picture. It gives one area where the husband has more power than the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father's control over his daughter's vows ends when she becomes a בוגרת, a grown woman. A husband who has fully married her keeps his power over her vows even after she becomes a בוגרת.

keyTerms.meaning: In another matter
Cancels (a vow)
Full adulthood, the stage after being a נערה

steps.whatToRemember: The father wins when the other one dies (he takes over). The husband wins when it comes to age (he can cancel even when she is a בוגרת).

phrases.english: In another matter, the husband's power is stronger
than the father's power:
for the husband cancels vows during her adulthood,
and the father does not cancel vows during her adulthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדָבָר אַחֵר יִפָּה כֹּחַ הַבַּעַל מִכֹּחַ הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the comparison started in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband can cancel vows of a בוגרת. A father cannot.

steps.title: Why the husband does not take over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's first rule: when the father dies, why doesn't the husband take over?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's first rule. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the first half of step 6: why the father's share does not pass to the husband when the father dies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the husband does not take over when the father dies.

steps.title: She stays in her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'בנעריה בית אביה': while she is a נערה, she is treated as in her father's house, even after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the verse says: 'In her youth, in her father's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. As long as she is a נערה, she is linked to her father's house, so the husband does not take over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties the girl's youth to her father's house. Even if the father dies, she is still seen as belonging to his house during her נערות, so the husband never gets full control during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the verse says
In her youth (while she is a נערה)
Her father's house

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"In her youth, in her father's house."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'בנעריה בית אביה' shows that during her נערות she stays under her father's house, even after his death.

steps.title: Source for the father taking over
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn the משנה's second rule, that when the husband dies the father takes over.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband died, the authority passes to the father. From where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of the other half of the rule. This sets up רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first source only explained why the husband cannot take over. A separate source is needed to show that the father does take over the husband's share.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: If the husband died, the authority passes over to the father:
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת הַבַּעַל נִתְרוֹקְנָה רְשׁוּת לָאָב מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the source of the first half of the rule to the source of the second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the father takes over when the husband dies.

steps.title: רבה brings the doubled wording 'היו תהיה'
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers from the פסוק 'ואם היו תהיה לאיש ונדריה עליה'. The doubled wording points to a girl betrothed more than once.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Because the verse says: 'And if she shall surely be to a man, and her vows are upon her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins to answer with a פסוק. His explanation of how the פסוק teaches this continues on the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה say 'be' twice. That hints at two betrothals, for example after a first husband dies. The point that the father takes over in such a case will be built from this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'She shall surely be', a doubled form of the word 'be'
And her vows are upon her

phrases.english: רבה said:
Because the verse says:
"And if she shall surely be to a man,
phrases.notes: במדבר 30:7. The word 'be' is doubled here, and that doubling is what רבה will build on.

phrases.english: and her vows are upon her"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה דְּאָמַר קְרָא וְאִם הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה לְאִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled wording הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה hints at two betrothals. This is the start of the source that the father takes over when the husband dies.
